# 0001 Personal greeting

## Problem
`greet()` in `src/greeting.js` takes no argument and always returns "Hello, world!", so callers cannot greet a specific person.

## Scope
In: `greet(name)` returns "Hello, <name>!"; falls back to "Hello, world!" when no name is given. Out: localization, name validation or trimming, any CLI or UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC-01: `greet("Ada")` returns "Hello, Ada!"
- [ ] AC-02: `greet()` returns "Hello, world!" (existing behavior preserved)

## Approach
Single change in `src/greeting.js`: add a `name` parameter defaulting to "world" and return `` `Hello, ${name}!` ``. Tests go in `test/greeting.test.js`, next to the existing "greets the world" test. Rejected: explicit `if (!name)` branching; a default parameter is simpler (empty string and null are out of scope).

## Open questions
- none
